statusText:
The CME weekend halt still governs the published state. NQ has not quoted since Friday's close and does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, so Tail stays at 12% (low), the action stays EA_ON and the status stays green: the pathological one-way price path that Tail measures cannot form while no venue is quoting.

Two things changed this hour, and both cut the same way. First, the diplomatic track has hardened further. Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi has now put a precondition on talks resuming at all - that Washington stop what Tehran calls its violations of June's memorandum of understanding and compensate for them - saying that until then "the possibility of resuming negotiations does not exist." Al Jazeera's Saturday coverage reports Tehran has made no decision on returning to the table. Last hour's reading was that the Iran-Oman shipping accord was not yet an off-ramp because Washington had refused its precondition; this hour the counterparty has added a precondition of its own to the prior question of whether there is a negotiation at all.

Second, the supply damage has been quantified by a credible neutral party. The IEA's August Oil Market Report, published 12 August, now projects a third-quarter 2026 global oil deficit of 1.8 million barrels per day - more than double last month's roughly 800,000 b/d estimate and the deepest quarterly shortfall since late 2021 - after cutting third-quarter supply by 1.7 million b/d on the July and early-August hostilities. It notes 8.3 million b/d of Gulf production still shut in and warns that "the urgency of reopening the Strait has increased, as previously available inventory buffers are rapidly depleting."

That is the entire tension of this weekend in one line: crude has repriced a structural supply deficit for a week, and equity volatility has not moved. WTI closed Friday at $82.40 (+1.42%, more than +5% on the week) and Brent at $88.52 (+1.67%), while NQ finished at 30,141.75 (-0.15%) and the VIX at 14.25, near the low end of its range. Stress rises to 74% to carry that divergence. Tail does not, because there is still no path to score.
recommendation:
Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 12% maps to EA_ON. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut - existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The actionable item is scheduling, not sizing.

The roughly 22:00 UTC restart sits inside this forecast window and is the single checkpoint that matters. Forecast Tail steps from 19% at 21:00 UTC to 23% at 22:00 UTC and 24% at 23:00 UTC, turning the forecast status yellow (WATCH) for the final five slots and easing to 21% by 02:00 UTC Monday. Treat that thin opening auction as the moment an entire weekend is priced at once: an undelivered Hezbollah retaliation, a negotiation track Tehran says cannot resume without US compensation, a third struck ADNOC vessel, Hormuz transits still running near a sixth of pre-conflict volume, and an IEA-verified 1.8 mb/d third-quarter crude deficit - against a 14-handle VIX that has discounted none of it. No US macro release lands inside the window; Monday's Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC is the first, and it is medium impact. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 12% and status green, but Tehran now conditions any resumption of talks on US compensation and the IEA has quantified a 1.8 mb/d third-quarter crude deficit, so Stress rises to 74% into tonight's 22:00 UTC CME restart
body:
Price path: none exists. The current hour and the first nineteen forecast slots all sit inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to extremes to score. Every price input is a Friday carry-forward. That is simultaneously the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit at 69% (solid) rather than in the high band.

Friday's marks, re-verified against primary sources this hour: NQ September futures 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15%, range 30,028.50-30,283.00 against a 30,188.50 previous close, with the quote page explicitly reporting the contract closed as of 14 August. VIX 14.25, -2.60%, range 14.18-14.72, also marked closed at 14 August. WTI $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%). US 2-year 4.15% and 10-year 4.63% from the Fed's H.15 release at the 13 August observation. Nothing in that cross-asset set is aligned into a one-way equity structure. Conflicting signals belong in Stress, not Tail.

The first new input this hour is diplomatic and it removes what little remained of the off-ramp. Last hour the assessment downgraded the Iran-Oman Hormuz shipping accord because its precondition - that Washington lift the blockade of Iranian ports - is the opposite of what the United States said on Thursday, when it warned it could maintain the blockade indefinitely and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent promised economic isolation of a kind not previously seen. This hour the symmetry completes: Araghchi has said the United States continues to violate June's memorandum of understanding and that until that ends and Washington compensates for what it has violated, "the possibility of resuming negotiations does not exist," while Al Jazeera's Saturday coverage reports Tehran has made no decision on returning to talks. Iran's stated terms for a war-ending deal now run to an end of US threats, a permanent halt to attacks on Iran and its allies, lifting of the naval blockade, withdrawal of US naval and air forces from around Iran, compensation for damage, sanctions relief and unconditional release of frozen assets. Meanwhile President Trump has said he will declare the Strait of Hormuz US territory "pretty soon" and a carrier group is en route to relieve the USS Lincoln. Neither side's stated position is currently reachable from the other's.

The second new input is quantitative and it is the more useful of the two. The IEA's August Oil Market Report, published 12 August, now puts the third-quarter 2026 global oil balance at a 1.8 million b/d deficit, more than double the roughly 800,000 b/d it estimated a month earlier, after cutting third-quarter supply projections by 1.7 million b/d on the renewed July and early-August hostilities. It marks 2026 demand down 510,000 b/d - an annual decline of 1.6 million b/d - which means the deficit is widening despite demand destruction, not because of demand strength. Roughly 8.3 million b/d of Gulf production remains shut in, and the agency's language is unusually direct: the urgency of reopening the strait has increased because inventory buffers are rapidly depleting. Separately, UKMTO transit counts put Hormuz traffic at roughly 17% of the pre-conflict average over the past seven days, about 151 vessels, versus roughly 130 transits a day before the conflict.

That matters for a Nasdaq risk state because it converts a headline stream into a measurable, persistent supply shortfall with a depleting buffer - the kind of input that can eventually reprice discount rates and margins rather than just the energy complex. It has not done so yet. Equity volatility remains unmoved: the VIX closed at 14.25 near the low end of its 52-week range and the Nasdaq Composite finished Friday about 0.3% lower while still closing the week higher. When one asset class prices a structural supply deficit and another prices nothing, the honest place to record the gap is Stress, and the honest reading is that equities carry unhedged headline exposure into a thin reopening auction.

Lebanon is unchanged from last hour and still unresolved. Hezbollah said Israel's strikes - eleven killed at Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani including three children and two women, the deadliest since the June de-escalation - "will be met with an appropriate response," with no timing or scope given, and told Lebanese authorities not to continue along the "humiliating path of direct negotiations" ahead of an eighth round of US-sponsored talks due in Rome early next month. A promised, undelivered retaliation combined with an explicit attempt to collapse the negotiating track is a two-part overhang, and neither part can decay while markets are shut.

Why Tail stays at 12% and not higher: Tail measures a pathological price path, not the size of a pending headline stack. There is no path. The full amplifier checklist - persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, NQ pinned near an extreme, aligned yields, VIX, oil, semis, megacaps and breadth - is unobservable and stays unobservable for roughly another eighteen and a half hours. Publishing an elevated Tail now would assert structure that no venue has produced.

Why Stress rises to 74% (high) rather than further: the escalation column gained two items this hour, one of which is a hard number from a neutral agency, and the de-escalation column gained nothing. Stress stays inside the high band rather than moving to extreme because no new physical incident was reported in this hour, because the Iran-Oman technical work on a safe corridor is still described as progressing, and because a large but recoverable drawdown - not a regime break - remains the correct characterisation of the risk to a mean-reversion basket.

The horizon geometry is fully engaged. From 03:00 UTC Sunday the 24-hour forecast reaches 02:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC restart and the first four hours after it sit inside the window. Forecast Tail therefore drifts 12% to 19% through the halt and then steps to 23%, 24%, 23%, 22% and 21% for the final five slots, where the forecast action becomes WATCH and the forecast status yellow. A thin opening auction absorbing an entire weekend at once is exactly the configuration in which gap continuation can outrun mean reversion. That is a conditional forecast, not an observation: the current published action remains EA_ON and green.

Confidence holds at 69% (solid). Two forces offset. Against it, Friday's price marks are now more than 100 hours old and the single most informative input for a mean-reversion strategy - live price path - is structurally unavailable until the restart. For it, the evidence set widened this hour rather than merely aging: index, volatility, energy and rate marks re-verified against primary sources and mutually consistent, a quantified supply balance from the IEA replacing qualitative reporting, and the seven-day US calendar re-read directly from Trading Economics confirming no US release of any kind before Monday's Empire State survey and no Fed event before Wednesday's FOMC minutes.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours run from 03:00 UTC Saturday to 02:00 UTC Sunday and are entirely inside the CME weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours. Tail never left the low band, drifting 9% to 12%. Stress is what actually moved: 45% through the Saturday Asian hours, then climbing steadily through 48%, 50%, 51%, 52%, 53%, 54%, 55%, 56%, 58%, 57%, 60%, 62%, 65%, 67%, 68%, 70%, 71% and 73% as the Lebanon strikes were confirmed and became a two-sided exchange, the Hormuz tanker attacks accumulated, and the Iran-Oman accord was re-read as conditional rather than a genuine off-ramp. Confidence rebuilt in parallel from 59% to 69% as primary-source marks were re-verified hour by hour. Action was EA_ON and status green for all 24 hours, and dominantMode was mixed throughout.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours end at 02:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC CME restart and the first four hours after it are inside the window. Tail is held in the low band for 19 of 24 slots, drifting 12% to 19% as the restart approaches, then stepping to 23% at 22:00 UTC, 24% at 23:00 UTC, 23% at 00:00 UTC, 22% at 01:00 UTC and 21% at 02:00 UTC Monday, where the forecast action becomes WATCH and the forecast status yellow. Stress grinds from 74% to a 79% plateau because unpriced weekend risk compounds while the venue is shut - an undelivered Hezbollah response, an explicit Hezbollah demand that Beirut abandon direct negotiations, Tehran conditioning any resumption of talks on US compensation, a Hormuz framework whose precondition Washington has publicly refused, and an IEA-quantified 1.8 mb/d third-quarter crude deficit with depleting inventory buffers - then eases to 75% once live price discovery starts converting headline risk into an actual mark. Confidence decays from 69% to 62% as Friday's marks age past 120 hours, then recovers to 68% once live quotes return at the reopen. The last six slots switch to event/whipsaw to reflect a thin opening auction that has to absorb the entire weekend at once.

forecastDetail.comment: Deep Asian-Sunday hours inside the CME weekend halt: no quote, no path, nothing for a reverse/grid basket to be caught by. Tail stays at 12% because the pathological structure it measures cannot form while every venue is shut. Stress holds at 74% - an undelivered Hezbollah retaliation, a negotiation track Tehran says cannot resume until Washington compensates, and an IEA-quantified 1.8 mb/d third-quarter crude deficit all sit unpriced.
Still fully inside the halt. Confidence slips a point to 68% purely on age: Friday's marks are now more than 100 hours old and no live tick can refresh them. Risk itself is unchanged.

Halt continues through the Asian Sunday morning. Watch for weekend headline flow out of Beirut and the Gulf rather than price; any confirmed Hezbollah response or a fresh Hormuz strike in this window would land straight into Sunday's thin reopening auction.
Stress ticks to 75% as the unpriced weekend stack ages another hour without an offsetting de-escalation headline. Tail unchanged at 12% - still no observable price path.

Early European Sunday. Tail edges to 13%, the first small acknowledgement that the restart is drawing closer and that gap risk is beginning to be a forecastable object rather than a purely hypothetical one. Action stays EA_ON.

Halt persists. Confidence 67% and drifting as the mark set ages; the assessment is now almost entirely event-driven rather than structure-driven, which is exactly the configuration in which Stress, not Tail, should carry the weight.
